explain.say: Every human eye has a small patch where it cannot see anything at all. It is called the blind spot, and it comes from the way the eye is wired.

faq.a: The blind spot is the place on the retina where the optic nerve leaves the eye. It has no rods or cones, so any light that lands there cannot be seen.
asks: Why is there a blind spot in the eye?

faq.q: Why don't I notice my blind spot?
faq.a: Your two eyes have blind spots in different places, so each covers the other's gap. Even with one eye shut, the brain fills the hole with whatever pattern surrounds it.
asks: Why can't I see a hole in my vision?
How does the brain fill in the blind spot?

faq.q: How can I find my blind spot?
faq.a: Draw a cross and a dot about 8 centimetres apart. Close your left eye, stare at the cross with your right eye, and slowly move the paper towards you: at one distance the dot vanishes.
asks: How do you see your blind spot?

faq.a: The optic nerve is a cable of about a million nerve fibres that carries signals from the retina to the brain. Where it leaves the eye is the blind spot.
asks: What does the optic nerve do?
How do signals get from the eye to the brain?

faq.q: Does every eye have a blind spot?
faq.a: Every human eye does, and so do the eyes of other animals with backbones. Octopus and squid eyes are wired the other way, with nerves behind the retina, so they have no blind spot.
asks: Why do octopuses not have a blind spot?

facts: The optic nerve contains roughly one million nerve fibres.
The blind spot sits about 15 degrees to the side of where you are looking, towards the nose side of the retina.

options.show: It has no rods or cones where the optic nerve leaves

options.say: It is covered by the iris

quiz.why: All the nerve fibres leave the eye at one spot, the optic disc, and there is no room there for light-sensing cells.

wrong.1: Light can reach the spot; there is just nothing there to detect it.
wrong.2: The iris is at the front of the eye, far from the retina.
